author_note: independent reference authored without access to the tool code
reference: Hand-built electrical safe-work plans (EU, US and site rule packs; LV AC/DC, ELV and HV; complete plans, each core step removed, wrong order, unsuitable instruments, environment flags, adjacent live parts, stored energy, backfeed, energized exceptional path, insufficient and malformed data) plus IEC band boundary cases and 12 seeded random voltages classified by an own threshold function (ref.py). Categorical expectations follow EN 50110-1:2023 clause 6.2 structure, HSE HSG85 and GS38, 29 CFR 1910.333, IEC 61140 band limits, or the spec's acceptance criteria.
reference_citations: HSE HSG85 'Electricity at work: Safe working practices', 3rd ed. 2013, https://www.hse.gov.uk/pubnS/priced/hsg85.pdf - paras 23, 47, 48, 49, 52, 53, 55, 57, 59
HSE GS38 'Electrical test equipment for use on low voltage electrical systems', 4th ed., https://www.hse.gov.uk/pubns/priced/gs38.pdf - paras 13, 17, 19, 20
EN 50110-1:2023 clause 6.2 headings 6.2.2-6.2.6 (publisher sample ToC only; body text not read) https://cdn.standards.iteh.ai/samples/70639/d56b2cf915854d53975e552586b1b839/SIST-EN-50110-1-2023.pdf
IEC 61140 ELV/LV limits as reported (secondary) by https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extra-low_voltage and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low_voltage (standard itself not read)
Spec specs/12.md (acceptance criteria) and specs/00-common.md (insufficient-data rule)
tolerance: exact for every check: all outputs are categorical (outcome, voltage band) or boolean properties of a rule engine; the only numbers are thresholds compared with <=, so any deviation is a logic difference. Band boundaries are inclusive (<= limit) as the sources state 'does not exceed'.
